record.field: CRA prescribed rate - taxable benefits on loans

Annual prescribed interest rate used to compute the deemed interest benefit on interest-free and low-interest loans to shareholders and employees, one version per calendar quarter. Income Tax Regulations s. 4301(c); ITA s. 80.4(2), 80.4(7). Revenu Quebec applies the same rate to the equivalent Quebec benefit. Source: https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/prescribed-interest-rates/2026-q4.html (and the page of each quarter).

Number of years after the end of the lender's taxation year in which the loan was made within which the loan must be repaid to avoid the income inclusion. ITA s. 15(2.6). Source: https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/I-3.3/section-15.html
Deemed interest - days to pay interest

Interest on a shareholder loan paid not later than this number of days after the end of the calendar year reduces the deemed interest benefit. ITA s. 80.4(1)(c), 80.4(2)(b). Source: https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/I-3.3/section-80.4.html
Quebec SBD - remunerated hours lower threshold

Total remunerated hours at or below which the Quebec small business deduction rate is nil; the rate grows linearly up to the upper threshold. Taxation Act (Quebec) s. 771.2.1.2; Quebec Information Bulletin 2026-3, section 1. Source: https://cdn-contenu.quebec.ca/cdn-contenu/adm/min/finances/publications-adm/Bulletins/EN/BULEN_2026-3.pdf
Quebec SBD - remunerated hours upper threshold

Total remunerated hours (the corporation's employees in the year, or the corporation and its associated corporations in the preceding year) from which the full Quebec small business deduction rate applies. Taxation Act (Quebec) s. 771.2.1.2; Quebec Information Bulletin 2026-3, section 1. Source: https://cdn-contenu.quebec.ca/cdn-contenu/adm/min/finances/publications-adm/Bulletins/EN/BULEN_2026-3.pdf
Quebec SBD - weekly hours counted per employee

Maximum number of hours per week counted for each employee in the remunerated hours of the Quebec small business deduction. Taxation Act (Quebec) s. 771.2.1.1 (definition of remunerated hours); Revenu Quebec form CO-771 instructions. Source: https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/online-services/forms-and-publications/current-details/co-771-ch/
Quebec SBD - majority shareholder hours factor

Multiplier of the hours that a person holding, directly or indirectly, the majority of the voting shares of the corporation works during the taxation year to take an active part in its business, when these hours are included in the remunerated hours of the Quebec small business deduction. All the hours worked count, paid or not. Revenu Quebec form CO-771, notes 2 and 3 to lines 07a and 07b. Source: https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/online-services/forms-and-publications/current-details/co-771-ch/
Quebec SBD - primary and manufacturing lower ratio

Proportion of primary and manufacturing sectors activities at or below which the sector criterion gives no Quebec small business deduction (linear up to the upper ratio). Quebec Information Bulletin 2026-3, section 1. Source: https://cdn-contenu.quebec.ca/cdn-contenu/adm/min/finances/publications-adm/Bulletins/EN/BULEN_2026-3.pdf
Quebec SBD - primary and manufacturing upper ratio

Proportion of primary and manufacturing sectors activities from which the sector criterion gives the full Quebec small business deduction rate. Quebec Information Bulletin 2026-3, section 1. Source: https://cdn-contenu.quebec.ca/cdn-contenu/adm/min/finances/publications-adm/Bulletins/EN/BULEN_2026-3.pdf

Basic rate of Part I tax on taxable income. ITA s. 123(1)(a). Sources: https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/I-3.3/section-123.html ; https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/corporations/corporation-tax-rates.html

Deduction for taxable income earned in a province. ITA s. 124(1). Sources: https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/I-3.3/section-124.html ; https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/corporations/corporation-tax-rates.html

General rate reduction on full rate taxable income. ITA s. 123.4(2). Sources: https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/I-3.3/section-123.4.html ; https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/corporations/corporation-tax-rates.html

Small business deduction rate for days after 2018 (net rate 9% after abatement). ITA s. 125(1.1). Sources: https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/I-3.3/section-125.html ; https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/corporations/corporation-tax-rates.html

Business limit of a CCPC not associated with another CCPC, also the denominator of the passive income grind. ITA s. 125(2), 125(5.1)(b). Source: https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/I-3.3/section-125.html
Business limit - short year in weeks
A taxation year shorter than this number of weeks prorates the business limit by days / 365. ITA s. 125(5)(b). Source: https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/I-3.3/section-125.html
Business limit grind - taxable capital lower

Taxable capital employed in Canada (associated group, preceding year) from which the business limit is reduced linearly. ITA s. 125(5.1)(a): A x 0.225% x (C - $10M) / $90,000. Source: https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/I-3.3/section-125.html
Business limit grind - taxable capital upper

Taxable capital at which the business limit reaches nil (0.225% x $40M = $90,000). ITA s. 125(5.1)(a), for taxation years beginning after April 6, 2022. Source: https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/I-3.3/section-125.html
Business limit grind - passive income threshold

Adjusted aggregate investment income of the preceding year above which the business limit is reduced. ITA s. 125(5.1)(b): D / $500,000 x 5 x (E - $50,000). Source: https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/I-3.3/section-125.html
Business limit grind - passive income multiplier
Reduction of the business limit per dollar of adjusted aggregate investment income above the threshold. ITA s. 125(5.1)(b). Source: https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/I-3.3/section-125.html
Federal additional tax on personal services business income

Additional tax on personal services business income; that income gets neither the small business deduction nor the general rate reduction. ITA s. 123.5. Source: https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/I-3.3/section-123.5.html
Federal additional refundable tax on investment income

10 2/3% of the lesser of aggregate investment income and taxable income in excess of the small business deduction base. ITA s. 123.3. Source: https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/I-3.3/section-123.3.html
Federal refundable portion of Part I tax

30 2/3% of aggregate investment income added to the non-eligible refundable dividend tax on hand. ITA s. 129(4) (definition of non-eligible refundable dividend tax on hand). Source: https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/I-3.3/section-129.html
Dividend refund per dollar of taxable dividends paid, limited by the refundable dividend tax on hand. ITA s. 129(1)(a). Source: https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/I-3.3/section-129.html

Deductible portion of food, beverages and entertainment expenses; the rest is added back to accounting income. ITA s. 67.1(1); Taxation Act (Quebec) s. 421.1. Source: https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/I-3.3/section-67.1.html
Federal balance-due - months after year end

The balance of Part I tax is due this number of months after the end of the taxation year. ITA s. 157(1)(b) and definition of balance-due day, s. 248(1). Sources: https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/I-3.3/section-248.html ; https://cpaquebec.ca/-/media/docs/developpement-professionnel/avis-experts/fiscalite-taxes-planification-financiere/guide_delais_fiscalite.pdf
Federal balance-due - months for a small CCPC

Balance-due delay for a CCPC throughout the year that claims the small business deduction and whose taxable income (associated group) of the preceding year does not exceed its business limit. ITA s. 248(1) balance-due day (d)(i). Sources: https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/I-3.3/section-248.html ; https://cpaquebec.ca/-/media/docs/developpement-professionnel/avis-experts/fiscalite-taxes-planification-financiere/guide_delais_fiscalite.pdf
Quebec balance - months after year end

The balance of Quebec income tax is due this number of months after the end of the taxation year. Taxation Act (Quebec) s. 1027. Source: https://cpaquebec.ca/-/media/docs/developpement-professionnel/avis-experts/fiscalite-taxes-planification-financiere/guide_delais_fiscalite.pdf
Quebec balance - months for a small CCPC

Quebec balance delay for a CCPC entitled to the small business deduction. The CPA Quebec deadline guide states 2 months in all cases for Quebec; set 3 if Revenu Quebec confirms the federal extension applies. Taxation Act (Quebec) s. 1027. Source: https://cpaquebec.ca/-/media/docs/developpement-professionnel/avis-experts/fiscalite-taxes-planification-financiere/guide_delais_fiscalite.pdf
Corporate return filing - months after year end

The T2 and CO-17 returns are due this number of months after the end of the taxation year. ITA s. 150(1)(a); Taxation Act (Quebec) s. 1000. Source: https://cpaquebec.ca/-/media/docs/developpement-professionnel/avis-experts/fiscalite-taxes-planification-financiere/guide_delais_fiscalite.pdf

No instalment is required when the tax of the year or the first instalment base (preceding year) does not exceed this amount. ITA s. 157(2.1). Source: https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/I-3.3/section-157.html
Quebec counterpart of the instalment threshold of corporations. Taxation Act (Quebec) s. 1027. Source: https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/businesses/income-tax/corporation-income-tax/

A small-CCPC may pay quarterly instalments when its taxable income (associated group) for the year or the preceding year does not exceed this amount. ITA s. 157(1.2)(a). Source: https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/I-3.3/section-157.html
Taxable capital employed in Canada (associated group) above which quarterly instalments are not available. ITA s. 157(1.2)(b). Source: https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/I-3.3/section-157.html
Quebec quarterly instalments - taxable income maximum

A CCPC may pay its Quebec instalments quarterly when its taxable income, including that of its associated corporations, for the current or the preceding taxation year does not exceed this amount, the other conditions being met. Guide CO-17.G, section 3.9.3: "son revenu imposable, y compris celui des sociétés associées, pour l'année d'imposition en cours ou pour l'année d'imposition précédente, ne dépasse pas 500 000 $". Taxation Act (Quebec) s. 1027. Source: https://www.revenuquebec.ca/fr/services-en-ligne/formulaires-et-publications/co-17-g/guide-de-la-declaration-de-revenus-des-societes/
Quebec quarterly instalments - paid-up capital maximum

A CCPC may pay its Quebec instalments quarterly when its paid-up capital, including that of its associated corporations, for the current or the preceding taxation year does not exceed this amount, the other conditions being met. Guide CO-17.G, section 3.9.3: "son capital versé, y compris celui des sociétés associées, pour l'année d'imposition en cours ou pour l'année d'imposition précédente, ne dépasse pas 10 millions de dollars". Taxation Act (Quebec) s. 1027. Source: https://www.revenuquebec.ca/fr/services-en-ligne/formulaires-et-publications/co-17-g/guide-de-la-declaration-de-revenus-des-societes/
General Quebec income tax rate of corporations. Taxation Act (Quebec) s. 771(1). Source: https://cdn-contenu.quebec.ca/cdn-contenu/adm/min/finances/publications-adm/Bulletins/EN/BULEN_2026-3.pdf

Maximum Quebec small business deduction rate (reduction of the general rate on eligible active business income), multiplied by the remunerated hours or sector factor. Read at the FIRST DAY of the taxation year: 8.3% (3.2% net) before; 9.3% (2.2% net) for taxation years starting after April 29, 2026 - announced in Quebec Information Bulletin 2026-3, legislation to follow. Taxation Act (Quebec) s. 771.2.1. Source: https://cdn-contenu.quebec.ca/cdn-contenu/adm/min/finances/publications-adm/Bulletins/EN/BULEN_2026-3.pdf

Quebec business limit of the small business deduction, before its proration for a short taxation year and its paid-up capital and passive income grinds (Revenu Quebec form CO-771, part 8.1). Taxation Act (Quebec) s. 771.2.1.2; Quebec Information Bulletin 2026-3, note 1. Source: https://cdn-contenu.quebec.ca/cdn-contenu/adm/min/finances/publications-adm/Bulletins/EN/BULEN_2026-3.pdf
Quebec business limit - short year in weeks

A taxation year shorter than this number of weeks prorates the Quebec business limit by days / 365, before the paid-up capital and passive income grinds. Revenu Quebec form CO-771, lines 76 to 80 and note 10; guide CO-17.G, section 4.4.3.9. Source: https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/online-services/forms-and-publications/current-details/co-771-ch/
Quebec business limit grind - paid-up capital lower

Paid-up capital (the corporation and its associated corporations, last taxation year ended in the preceding calendar year; amount J of form CO-771) above which the Quebec business limit is reduced linearly, for taxation years beginning on or after April 7, 2022. Revenu Quebec form CO-771, lines 84 to 95; guide CO-17.G, section 4.4.3.9. Source: https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/online-services/forms-and-publications/current-details/co-771-ch/
Quebec business limit grind - paid-up capital upper

Paid-up capital (amount J of form CO-771) from which the Quebec business limit is nil, for taxation years beginning on or after April 7, 2022 (reduction: (J - lower) / 40 million x the business limit). Revenu Quebec form CO-771, lines 84 to 95 and note 11; guide CO-17.G, section 4.4.3.9. Source: https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/online-services/forms-and-publications/current-details/co-771-ch/
Gross-up of eligible dividends (taxable amount = 138% of the actual amount). ITA s. 82(1)(b)(ii). Source: https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/I-3.3/section-82.html
Federal gross-up - other than eligible dividends
Gross-up of other than eligible dividends for 2019 and later (taxable amount = 115%). ITA s. 82(1)(b)(i). Source: https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/I-3.3/section-82.html

Federal dividend tax credit as a fraction of the taxable amount of eligible dividends: 6/11 of the gross-up = 15.0198% of the taxable amount (T5 box 26). ITA s. 121(b). Source: https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/I-3.3/section-121.html
Federal dividend tax credit - other than eligible

Federal dividend tax credit as a fraction of the taxable amount of other than eligible dividends: 9/13 of the gross-up = 9.0301% of the taxable amount (T5 box 12). ITA s. 121(a). Source: https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/I-3.3/section-121.html

Quebec gross-up of eligible dividends (RL-3 box B). Taxation Act (Quebec) s. 497. Source: https://www.revenuquebec.ca/fr/citoyens/declaration-de-revenus/produire-votre-declaration-de-revenus/comment-remplir-votre-declaration-de-revenus/aide-par-ligne/400-a-447-impot-et-cotisations/ligne-415/

Quebec gross-up of ordinary (other than eligible) dividends; unchanged by Quebec Information Bulletin 2026-3. Taxation Act (Quebec) s. 497. Source: https://cdn-contenu.quebec.ca/cdn-contenu/adm/min/finances/publications-adm/Bulletins/EN/BULEN_2026-3.pdf

Quebec dividend tax credit on eligible dividends: 11.7% of the taxable amount (16.146% of the actual amount, RL-3 box C). Taxation Act (Quebec) s. 767. Source: https://www.revenuquebec.ca/fr/citoyens/declaration-de-revenus/produire-votre-declaration-de-revenus/comment-remplir-votre-declaration-de-revenus/aide-par-ligne/400-a-447-impot-et-cotisations/ligne-415/

Quebec dividend tax credit on ordinary dividends as a fraction of the taxable amount, read at the payment date: 3.42% (3.933% of the actual amount); 2.69% (3.09% of the actual amount) for dividends received after December 31, 2026 - announced in Quebec Information Bulletin 2026-3, legislation to follow. Taxation Act (Quebec) s. 767. Source: https://cdn-contenu.quebec.ca/cdn-contenu/adm/min/finances/publications-adm/Bulletins/EN/BULEN_2026-3.pdf

A T5 slip is not required for a recipient whose total amount for the calendar year is less than this amount. Administrative threshold of the CRA T5 guide (T4015, "When you do not have to prepare a T5 slip"); Income Tax Regulations s. 201 itself sets no amount. Source: https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/forms-publications/publications/t4015/t5-guide-return-investment-income.html
